absent: Wire XDR field order, padding and version-specific encoding rules for the described records.
Lock ordering and sleep versus atomic context constraints beyond the stated client-lock and delegation-lock protection.
Delegation recall, return and lease-renewal sequencing, timeouts and failure recovery.
Layout driver internals, device address decoding and private blob formats.
Mount parsing, validation and negotiation that produce flags, sizes, timeouts and capability masks.
Error retry, failover, migration recovery and server-side copy fallback behaviour.

findings.text: A server record describes one mounted filesystem instance and groups communication handles, enumeration links, accounting, tuning and identity. It references shared client context, normal and ACL RPC endpoints, optional lock-manager state, per-CPU I/O counters, congestion signalling and backpressure counters, capability and option words, read and write extents, directory and block sizing, attribute-cache horizons, filesystem identity and limits, auth material, mount-daemon endpoint data, credential and sysfs lifetime, plus version-four attribute masks, layout driver selection, open-owner tracking, delegation collections, copy tracking, migration progress and a teardown hook.

Fifteen internal mount toggles each occupy one distinct high bit in the flags word, doubling from 0x10000 up to 0x40000000. They independently select negative-cache suppression versus no caching, unprivileged source port, legacy interface mode, local flock versus local fcntl handling, soft errors, soft revalidation, eager versus waiting writes, trunk discovery, shutdown, unaligned-write permission, forced directory-plus and fatal handling of network-unreachable.

Automount inheritance uses three low bits with values 1, 2 and 4 to propagate block size and read and write sizes to submounts. An extra options word uses value 1 to record local caching enablement and value 2 to record version-four migration enablement. Each bit is independent and combines by bitwise or.

File-handle volatility uses values 1 for no-expire-with-open, 2 for any volatility, 4 for migration volatility and 8 for rename volatility, with rename-unsafe defined as the combination of any-volatility and rename-volatility. A delegation-expired marker uses value 1. Migration progress uses 1 for in-transition, 2 for failed and 3 for transparent-state-migration possible.

Thirty-two server capabilities fill bits 0 through 31 of a capability word, each bit advertising one optional behaviour such as directory-plus, hardlink and symlink support, ACLs, atomic open variants, large open, case handling modes, layout return on reboot, offload status and cancel, zero range, directory delegation, exclusive-or open, delegation time, POSIX locking, identity mapping suppression, version-4.1 stateids, security labels, seek, allocate, deallocate, layout statistics, clone, copy, layout error, copy notify, extended attributes, read-plus, filesystem locations and movability.

A length-prefixed byte holder pairs an unsigned length with a character pointer for owner and group names. A filesystem identity pairs two 64-bit integers for major and minor components. A threshold hint carries a bitmap, a layout kind and four 64-bit sizes describing read and write extents and I/O granularities for migration or striping guidance.

File I/O bounds are 1048576 maximum, 4096 default and 1024 minimum. Attribute bitmaps use width 3. At most 8 layout types may be advertised. A layout blob is bounded by 4096 and a layout-statistics blob by 384. At most 5 layout errors may be reported together. An auxiliary flag marks uncacheable file data with bit 0.

A small equality helper reports whether two filesystem identities denote the same filesystem by requiring both major and minor components to match. It has no side effects, performs no locking and is safe in any context where its two inputs remain valid.

A cached attribute record is gated by a 64-bit validity word where each bit authorises one field. It stores mode, link count, owner, group, device identity, size, space-use detail that varies by protocol version, filesystem identity, file and mounted-on identifiers, access and modification and change and birth times, auxiliary version-four flags, current and pre-operation change values, pre-operation size and times, cache timing and generation, optional owner and group strings, optional threshold hints and optional security label.

Twenty-eight attribute-validity bits occupy positions 0 through 27 of a 64-bit word, each naming one cacheable property such as type, mode, link count, owner, group, device, size, pre-size, block versus space use, filesystem identity, file identity, three main times, pre-operation times, change and pre-change values, location and referral data, mountpoint and mounted-on identity, owner and group names, security label, birth time and uncacheable-data marking. A core set combines the common stable attributes, with version-two adding block use, version-three adding space use and version-four further adding space use, birth time, security label and uncacheable marking.

Filesystem interrogation results share a pattern of pairing an optional post-operation attribute pointer with operation-specific measurements. One record reports transfer maxima, preferences and multiples, directory preference, maximum file size, time granularity, lease duration, layout-type inventory, block sizes, clone granularity, change-attribute description and extended-attribute support. Others report byte and file totals with free and available splits, version-two block counts with transfer size, link and name limits with case behaviour, and a change wrapper with atomicity flag plus before and after counters.

Session tuning is conveyed as five unsigned maxima for request size, response size, cached response size, operations and outstanding requests. Every sequenced compound pairs a small argument carrying a slot reference plus cache-this and privileged markers with a result carrying slot-operation hooks, the used slot, a timestamp, operation status, status flags and highest-slot identifiers. Lease-time probing wraps this sequencing pair with no extra arguments and returns filesystem info alongside the sequence result.

Layout-private extensibility uses an operation pair for encoding and release plus a holder that binds those operations to untyped data. Driver payloads are described as page arrays with page length and byte length. A layout extent is described by an I/O mode with offset and length. Together these let distinct layout types transport private blobs without changing the generic scaffolding.

Layout negotiation follows a get, device-info, commit and return cycle, each stage pairing sequenced arguments with sequenced results and state identifiers. Get specifies type, desired range, minimum length, maximum count and open context and returns status, return-on-close policy, granted range and driver blob. Device-info names a device and notification interest and returns notification state. Commit reports bytes written with attribute mask and update pages and returns post-operation attributes and status. Return identifies layout, range and type with private data and returns presence indication and fresh state.

Per-device statistics record device identity, byte interval, read and write operation counts and byte totals, layout type and private encoding, transported in counted arrays with inode and handle context. Error reporting pairs offsets and lengths with state identifiers and per-device entries that carry device identity, status and failed operation number. Server-side copy names source and destination handles and state identifiers with source and destination offsets, length and destination attribute mask, returning operation status and destination attributes.

Open-owner identity combines creation time with a uniquifier. Delegation outcome is a discriminated variant that either grants a recallable delegation with access mode, recall flag, state and page-modification limit or explains denial with reason and future-notification promise. Open arguments carry sequencing, handle, sequence identifier, flags, mode, share and access requests, client identity, owner identity, a claim-dependent variant for creation attributes with verifier versus delegation versus previous-claim type, name, server for identity mapping, attribute masks, claim and creation modes, label, umask and optional layout request, with results returning state, handle, change info, flags, attributes, sequence state, attribute presence, owner strings, delegation, access negotiation and optional layout response. Confirmation is a narrow exchange of handle, state and sequence identifier returning refreshed state.

Open-owner tracking under version four is guarded by the shared client lock. Delegation collections are guarded by a dedicated spin lock in the server record. Writeback accounting uses atomic counters with a wait queue and congested flag for backpressure. Active-delegation and activity counts use atomics, generation counters track delegation and migration epochs, and reclamation is deferred through RCU with sysfs and credential references defining lifetime.

Several pairing and bound rules hold throughout. A validity bit must be set before its attribute field is trusted. Attribute and server bitmap arrays have width three. Advertised layout-type count never exceeds eight and reported layout-error count never exceeds five. Each sequence argument has a matching sequence result sharing the same slot. Post-operation attribute pointers accompany info, stat, pathconf, commit and copy results. Change info always carries atomicity plus before and after values. Delegation and migration flag words only take their enumerated small values.

Several states require cautious handling. Handles marked volatile or migration- or rename-sensitive must not be assumed stable across operations. Migration failure is distinct from transitional state and from possible transparent migration. An expired-delegation marker forces revalidation rather than continued use. A shutdown toggle stops further activity. Excess writeback sets congestion and waiters must sleep until eased. Data flagged uncacheable must bypass caching even when other attributes appear valid.

Three provider hooks allow custom behaviour. A server teardown callback releases per-filesystem resources. An opaque pair supplies encode and release operations for layout-private data carried inside generic compounds. A statistics encoder serialises per-device layout statistics into wire form. Callers supply context and buffers while providers implement the type-specific logic.

Migration occupies one of three exclusive conditions: transitional, failed or transparent-migration possible, advanced by migration events rather than combined. Delegation outcome is exclusive between granted with possible recall and denied with reason and notification promise. Layout lifecycle advances from acquisition through optional device resolution and commit to return, with return-on-close as an early-release path.
A header inclusion guard macro ensures the wire-type header is processed at most once per translation unit, preventing duplicate definitions when multiple headers include it directly or indirectly.
